From ed46f39c47eb5530a9c161481a2080d3a869cfaf Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Cl=C3=A9ment=20L=C3=A9ger?= <cleger@meta.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:07:13 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] io_uring/net: inherit IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE across bundle
 recv retries
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

When a bundle recv retries inside io_recv_finish(), the merge logic OR
the saved cflags from the previous iteration with the cflags returned by
the new iteration:
  cflags = req->cqe.flags | (cflags & CQE_F_MASK);

Bits listed in CQE_F_MASK are inherited from the new iteration, and all
other bits (notably IORING_CQE_F_BUFFER and the buffer ID) come from the
saved cflags. Before this change CQE_F_MASK covered only
IORING_CQE_F_SOCK_NONEMPTY and IORING_CQE_F_MORE.

When using provided buffer rings (IOU_PBUF_RING_INC) with incremental
mode, and bundle recv, io_kbuf_inc_commit() can leave the head ring
entry partially consumed, __io_put_kbufs() then sets
IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE on the returned cflags so userspace knows the
buffer ID will be reused for subsequent completions.

Because IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE was not in CQE_F_MASK, the merge above
silently dropped it whenever the final retry iteration partially
consumed the buffer, and the subsequent req->cqe.flags = cflags &
~CQE_F_MASK save would have left a stale IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE in the
carried-over cflags had one been present. Userspace would then
wrongfully advance it ring head past an entry the kernel still uses.

Add IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE to CQE_F_MASK so it is both inherited from the
new iteration into the user-visible CQE and stripped from the saved
cflags between iterations.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Clément Léger <cleger@meta.com>
Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-4.6
Fixes: ae98dbf43d75 ("io_uring/kbuf: add support for incremental buffer consumption")
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260604160715.2482972-1-cleger@meta.com
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/io_uring/net.c b/io_uring/net.c
index 8df15b639358..ee848eb65ec9 100644
--- a/io_uring/net.c
+++ b/io_uring/net.c
@@ -842,7 +842,8 @@ int io_recvmsg_prep(struct io_kiocb *req, const struct io_uring_sqe *sqe)
 }
 
 /* bits to clear in old and inherit in new cflags on bundle retry */
-#define CQE_F_MASK	(IORING_CQE_F_SOCK_NONEMPTY|IORING_CQE_F_MORE)
+#define CQE_F_MASK	(IORING_CQE_F_SOCK_NONEMPTY|IORING_CQE_F_MORE|\
+			 IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE)
 
 /*
  * Finishes io_recv and io_recvmsg.
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a bug in the `io_uring/net` fast path where the `IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE` flag was silently dropped during bundle receive retries, leading to incorrect buffer ring head advancement in userspace.

**Modifications:**

- **File: `io_uring/net.c`**  
  - Updated the `CQE_F_MASK` macro (line 845) to include `IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE` alongside the existing `IORING_CQE_F_SOCK_NONEMPTY` and `IORING_CQE_F_MORE`.

**Relationship:**

The `CQE_F_MASK` is used in `io_recv_finish()` to merge completion flags (`cflags`) across bundle retry iterations. Bits in the mask are inherited from the new iteration; all other bits (including `IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE`) were previously taken from the saved `cflags` of the previous iteration. The missing flag caused the merge to drop `IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE` from the final CQE, while a stale value could remain in the saved `cflags`. By adding `IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE` to the mask, the flag is correctly inherited from each new iteration and properly cleared from the saved state, ensuring consistent propagation to userspace.

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs in the bundle recv retry logic in `io_recv_finish()` where the `CQE_F_MASK` macro omitted `IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE`. During retry, the merge operation `cflags = req->cqe.flags | (cflags & CQE_F_MASK)` incorrectly inherited flags from the new iteration only for bits in the mask, while `IORING_CQE_F_BUF_MORE` (which indicates the buffer ID will be reused) was taken from the previous saved `cflags`. This caused the flag to be silently dropped or carry a stale value, leading userspace to wrongly advance the buffer ring head when a bundle recv partially consumed a buffer in incremental mode, resulting in kernel/userspace buffer state mismatch.
